_evidence: Coherent block pool for the allocator 0x005387dc (0x400 slots of 0x18 bytes at 0x829cac; used end [0x82fcac], limit [0x82fcb0], serial [0x82fcb4]). The pool init 0x53873a sets every slot's +0 to its index k ('mov [edx],eax; ... inc eax' over 0x400 slots) and clears +8/+0xc; nothing else writes +0, so +0 = k is an invariant (the handle 0x538855 returns is +0 | serial<<10). The allocator gives a block start +8 = used end and length +0xc and advances the used end; 0x538921 (evict) moves [start+len, used end) down to start with 'rep movsb', ecx = [0x82fcac] - (start+len) (negative when a block reaches past the used end: the fault the old pool_005389b9+full_00538971 model hit at 0x538944, since full_00538971 gave slots >= 4 random lengths at start 0), then lowers every in-use start >= start and the used end by len. So in every reachable state the in-use blocks are disjoint and inside [base, used end), and the used end never exceeds the limit (a fit needs used+size <= limit, unsigned; evictions only lower it; the init sets used = base, limit = base + size via 0x538771). Model: slot k's block starts at 0xa06000 + 4k (the unreferenced zero-initialised .data stretch already used by pool_00538921/pool_005389b9; no instruction references 0xa05c40..0xa48cd8) with length +0xc from {1,2,3,4}, the first n slots in use (prefix n in {0,1,2,3,5,0x10,0x3ff,0x400,0x400}: 0x538971 finds slot n free, or none when n = 0x400 - the 0x53882c taken path), used end 0xa07000 (>= every start+len; gaps between blocks are allowed and keep every move count >= 0, and compaction preserves start+len <= used end for all remaining blocks), cache bytes 0xa06000..0xa07000 varied so the moves are visible. Limit >= used end (the invariant) from {+0,+0,+1,+4,+8,+0x10,+0x100,0xffffffff}. +0x14 (last use; evictable by 0x5388ed when below the running limit [0x82fcb4], then the chosen slot's +4) from both sides of the serial range 1024..4096, +4 any of 0..0x400000; the serial is drawn 1024..4096 here and serial_005387dc (composed last) gives the wrap value 0x3fffff (0x538991 then marks every in-use slot +0x14 = 1, serial = 2: all evictable). Requests (spec eax) are scaled to this 4 KB model: 0..0x10 bytes plus the wrap-around sizes 0xfffffff0/0xffffffff, so the overflow eax + used - limit is at most 0x10 and a call makes at most 16 evictions (each frees >= 1 byte); a request larger than the whole cache only repeats the same eviction loop (with n small and a tight limit the loop already exhausts the evictable slots and returns 0 - the 0x53881b taken path).
